items.title: Unmasking misogyny: How a Malayalam YouTube channel weaponises science against women
items.summary: In July 2026, during a debate on 24 News’ Thammil Thammil about whether women should face restrictions on what they wear, a woman panellist posed a question that cut to the heart of the argument: If women’s clothes provoke sexual assault, what explains the rape of children and elderly women? Muhammed Ameer, an ‘educator’ and one of the prominent faces of the Malayalam digital platform Unmasking Anomalies (UA), had an answer. “Consider”, he said, “the amount of sexual imagery men are exposed to every day, from hoardings and advertisements to models.” A man sees a sexually exposed woman and becomes sexually frustrated. Just as someone who cannot shout back at a boss might take their anger out on someone at home, he argued, sexual frustration can be taken out on a different target. This, Ameer said, was “frustration-aggression theory”. When another panellist objected that this did not explain why women should change what they wear, Ameer was emphatic. “This is a psychological theory,” he asserted. “It’s not me saying this.” It is an effective way to make an argument, enough to make the person sitting across from you in a debate pause and reconsider what they can immediately challenge.
